Thumbs up for true, thumbs down for false. Then click.

True

2. The monster burned the queen.

False: it saved her

3. The queen was a murderer.

False

True

True

False
02
Step 2 · Words to know · 2 min

Before we read

  • make allowances for: treat someone differently because of their problems
  • landmines: hidden bombs; here, things everyone is scared to step on
  • invisible: impossible to see
  • charisma: charm that makes people like you
  • ominously: in a threatening way
  • flinch: move suddenly because you are scared of being hit
  • cataclysmically: hugely, disastrously
  • relented: became less strict
  • a bird of prey: a hunting bird, like a hawk
  • a fortnight: two weeks

Step 6 · Chapter 10 questions · 9 min · in your book · full sentences

Chapter 10: "Understanding"

1 / 3
1

What does Lily forgive Conor for, and how does he answer?

Start: Lily forgives Conor for... but Conor says...
Look at the start of the chapter: "I forgive you for..."
She forgives him for getting her into trouble and for lying. Conor says he is not sorry and does not forgive her.
2

Lily says her mum told her to "make allowances" for Conor. Why does this make him so angry?

Start: This makes Conor angry because...
"Make allowances" means treating someone differently because of their problems.
He hates being treated differently because of his mum's illness. He wants people to treat him normally.
3

How did school change for Conor after people found out about his mum?

Start: After people found out, ...
Look for "It was like he'd suddenly turned invisible."
People stopped talking when he came over and whispered about him, so he stopped joining in and putting up his hand. He felt "invisible".
4

Harry raises his fist but does not punch Conor. What does Conor do, and what might Harry have worked out?

Start: Conor does not... so Harry may have worked out that...
Look for "Conor still didn't flinch." Then Harry says, "That's what I thought."
Conor does not flinch or move. Harry seems to work out that Conor wants to be hit, so hitting him would not hurt him the way Harry wants.
5

Miss Kwan lets Conor off. Why does this make him "feel even worse"?

Start: Being let off makes Conor feel worse because...
He thinks he could "stay out there all day and no one would punish him". Is that a good feeling?
Nobody treats him normally any more: he is so "invisible" that he will not even be punished. Part of him feels he does not deserve kindness.
07
Step 7 · Chapter 11 questions · 9 min · in your book · full sentences

Chapter 11: "Little Talk"

1 / 3
6

What news does Grandma give Conor when he gets home?

Start: Grandma tells Conor that...
There are three pieces of news: Mum, Conor, and Dad.
Mum has to go back to hospital, Conor will stay with Grandma for a few days, and his dad is flying in on Sunday.
7

Why is Conor surprised that his dad is coming?

Start: Conor is surprised because his dad...
Look for "Who hadn't come since..."
His dad has not visited since the Christmas before last. His visits and phone calls have become rarer since his new baby was born.
8

What does Mum tell Conor about her treatment?

Start: Mum tells Conor that...
Look for "This latest treatment's not..."
She says the latest treatment is "not doing what it's supposed to", but the doctors will try something else, so he should not worry.
9

Mum asks Conor to "Keep an eye on" the yew tree while she is away. What is she really telling him?

Start: She is really telling him that...
Read the next sentence: "And Conor knew this was her way of..."
She is telling him that she is coming back: "this was her way of telling him she was coming back".
10

Claim: Mum tries to protect Conor from bad news. Prove it with one short, exact quote from Chapter 11.

Start: Mum tries to protect Conor. She tells him, "..."
Use Tuesday's rule: relevant, short, exact. Look at what Mum says after "Look at me, son".
Any short, exact quote that proves it, for example: "There's lots more they can do. It's normal. Don't worry." or "I'm going to be okay," she said. "I really am."
